applicable_failures: The agent claimed 31 matters from one filename-regex script, but the output shown covers only a subset (e.g., 1001-00004, 1002-00001, 1003-00002, 1008-00002). The regex excluded 'generic' terms, so matters with other file naming were never listed.

Many matters that surfaced in earlier searches remain unlisted: 1045-00004 to 1045-00007, 1046-00001, 1005-00001, 1005-00002, 1021-00001 to 1021-00003, 1036-00001 and others. The pre-filtered pattern means the candidate set is hand-picked rather than complete.

The listing includes non-underwriting hits: 1001-00004 matched only a registration-rights agreement and 1003-00002 only fund subscription documents. Matching on filename alone gave weak classification and no full folder listings.
critique.concerns: The goal was complete file lists per candidate matter, but the script printed only files matching a name regex ('strong_files'), not full folder contents. Dozens of previously surfaced matters have no folder listing. The 31-matter claim is unsupported by the visible output, and shelved or never-executed matters with unusual file names would be missed. The self-assessment is overstated.
critique.recommendation: Re-run a full directory listing (no name regex, no cap) for every matter in the surfaced-but-unlisted set, printing all file names per matter, writing to a file and viewing it in chunks. Then judge candidates from complete listings, including draft-only and termination files.
